title: Juniper and the House
premise: Pest controller Ivo Halloran is called to Juniper House, where something inside leaves human fingerprints on the windows and counts its doors at night. There she finds Wren, the imaginary friend she invented as a child in 1974 and abandoned—still waiting, unchanged, feeding on the house's borrowed memories. Ivo learns the house took her sister's voice that year as payment for Wren's existence, and that staying invisible to it was the only thing keeping her alive. To free her sister, Ivo must return what was taken: she gives Wren back the childhood that created her, unmaking herself in the process, until her sister's remembered love calls her home and the house, finally uncounted, lets them both go.
about_author: Sable Crane is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent a decade cataloguing the strange maintenance requests of old houses. She writes horror about the debts buildings remember and the people who owe them.

chapters.title: The Call-Out
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. A routine pest complaint at derelict Juniper House turns strange: no droppings, no nests, only small human fingerprints dusted across the inside of every window. Ivo, who never takes night jobs, agrees to stay until morning. The emotional beat is professional detachment beginning to crack as she realizes the prints match no animal—and feel eerily familiar.

chapters.title: Doors, Counted
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Ivo keeps the lights on and counts the doors as her old habit demands, but the count keeps coming out wrong—one extra, then one missing. She finds her own childhood chalk drawings in a sealed room, dated 1974. The beat is dread sharpening into recognition: this house knows her, and she has been here before.

chapters.title: Wren on the Porch
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. At dusk, Wren—her childhood imaginary friend, exactly as drawn, unchanged by fifty years—is waiting on the porch, delighted. Wren speaks in Ivo's own six-year-old voice, recalling games Ivo barely remembers. The beat is vertigo and a shameful flicker of belonging, the first warmth Ivo has felt in decades, which frightens her more than the house.

chapters.title: What the House Ate
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Researching the Halloran family's 1974 tenancy, Ivo finds her sister Maren's name in a hospital intake record: elective mutism, onset that autumn. The house took Maren's voice as the price of Wren's existence. The beat is guilt igniting—loyalty to the friend who kept her lonely childhood bearable versus the truth that her play cost Maren everything.

chapters.title: The Tenant Below
chapters.summary: POV alternating Ivo and Wren. Wren's chapters reveal she is not Ivo's invention alone: the house dreamed her up using Ivo's loneliness, and she must be fed memories or she unravels. Wren has been keeping Maren's voice in the sealed room. The beat is tragic sympathy—Wren is both captor and captive, and she loves Ivo the way only a made thing can.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Ivo visits her sister, now in her sixties, mute since childhood but lucid. Maren writes a single sentence: 'You counted the doors wrong on purpose, so it would keep you.' Ivo realizes her lifelong compulsions were the house's leash, and that she has been its property all along. The beat is devastating clarity and the first decision to fight.

chapters.title: Uninvited
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Ivo tries to burn the chalk drawings and break the count, and the house retaliates—doors multiply, Wren appears in every window, and Ivo's reflection stops matching her movements. Wren begs her to stop, promising to give the voice back if Ivo stays forever. The beat is the loyalty-versus-truth collision at its sharpest: Wren's love is real, and it is a trap.

chapters.title: The Price of Returning
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren confesses the terms: the voice can be returned only by giving back what made her—Ivo's memories of 1974, of Wren herself. Ivo agrees, and begins forgetting her sister's illness, her own childhood, the reason she came. The beat is sacrificial tenderness as Ivo, losing herself, keeps only one thing: Maren's face.

chapters.title: The Sealed Room, Opened
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, fragmenting. Half-unmade, Ivo opens the sealed room and speaks Maren's voice back into the dark; the house convulses, its doors slamming open one by one as the count finally breaks. Wren, unraveling, chooses to spend her last coherence holding the house still while Ivo carries the voice out. The beat is the climax: grief, gratitude, and goodbye to the friend who was also a cage.

chapters.title: Counted, and Let Go
chapters.summary: POV Maren, her first. With her voice restored, Maren comes to the house and calls her sister's name—the one memory Ivo kept. The house, no longer owed anything, releases Ivo, who wakes on the porch with no childhood but a future. Juniper House stands empty, uncounted, its windows finally clean. The beat is bittersweet resolution: belonging found not in what was imagined, but in what was chosen.
